items.title: Is Iran ready for another major US attack after midterm elections?
items.summary: Tehran has said its goal is to keep the regime functioning and threaten enough regional costs to make a prolonged campaign unattractive. US media reports indicate Washington is considering strikes after the midterms The prospect of another major US attack is shaping calculations in Tehran, where officials are preparing for renewed strikes According to US media reports, the US and Israel have been examining new options for strikes against Iran The approaching US midterm elections on November 3, and Israel's election next week, have injected a political factor into how both countries are approaching the conflict they launched in late February Polls show high energy prices brought on by the Iran war are hurting Trump's Republicans. On October 8, Trump posted on social media that the US would not attack Iran before the midterms, citing "productive discussions" with Tehran.

items.title: Are Europeans putting profits over human rights in Vietnam?
items.summary: Europe and Vietnam are deepening economic and diplomatic ties, but closer cooperation raises concerns about whether Brussels is doing enough to address Hanoi's human rights record, labor standards and trade imbalances Vietnam 's Communist Party chief and president, To Lam , arrived in Brussels on Wednesday for an official visit to the European Union (EU) and Belgium in another sign of a relationship that continues to grow The visit comes just days after Vietnam signed a free trade agreement with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) , comprising Norway, Switzerland, Iceland and Liechtenstein Trade ties between Vietnam and Europe have deepened in recent years. The EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA), which took effect in August 2020 , substantially expanded Vietnam's commercial ties with most European states Amid global tariff wars, the EU-Vietnam relationship "is a welcome advertisement for keeping markets open," Khac Giang Nguyen, a visiting fellow at the ISEAS–Yusof Ishak Institute in Singapore, told DW "This is a win-win for both sides," he added.

items.title: Commercial banks sign agreements aimed at funding small businesses
items.summary: Maputo, 22 Oct (AIM) – Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has announced that six commercial banks have signed agreements to provide loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) under the Mutual Guarantee Fund. The fund, now valued at 120 million US dollars, is designed to facilitate access to credit for businesses that lack sufficient assets to secure bank loans. With support from the World Bank, the government provides guarantees to banks and assumes part of the risk if beneficiary businesses default on their repayments. “We are talking about a fund that now stands at 120 million US dollars. We stress the importance of expanding financing opportunities for businesses led by women, which often face obstacles in accessing bank credit”, he said. Chapo said that his government was also reviewing legal instruments to facilitate the participation of domestic businesses, particularly those led by women, in the supply chains of major investment projects.

items.title: Management of solar panel factory transferred to private company
items.summary: Maputo, 22 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican government has decided to transfer the management of Beluluane solar panel factory, which was managed by the country’s Energy Fund (FUNAE), to the Emirati Company Jampur Group. According to FUNAE chairman, Mety Gondola, the measure is aimed at modernizing the factory, which is located in Boane district, southern province of Maputo. The measure will also increase the capacity to supply equipment for the electrification of communities, particularly in rural areas. The management transfer was formalized on Wednesday through the signing of an agreement between the FUNAE and Jampur Group. Gondola explained that the decision to transfer management to the private sector stems, among other factors, from technological limitations that have constrained the industrial unit’s production capacity and competitiveness.

items.title: Two European women held captive for more than a year in Niger freed in Libya
items.summary: Eva Greztmacher, 76, had spent many years in Niger as an aid worker Two women - a Swiss and an Austrian – have been freed after more than a year in captivity in Niger and handed over to authorities in the Libyan city of Benghazi Austrian national Eva Gretzmacher, 76, and Swiss Claudia Abbt, 69, were kidnapped separately in the northern Nigerien city of Agadez in January and April last year No details have been given about who was holding them or their demands, although some reports have previously linked the kidnapping to Islamic State militants. The circumstances of their release were not disclosed The Austrian and Swiss governments have both confirmed the release of their citizens The Swiss government said Abbt was free and on her way back to Switzerland, while Austria said Gretzmacher had been released after "intensive diplomatic efforts" "We are all very relieved that Eva G. is free again after more than 21 months... For many months, we worked closely, discreetly, and in a spirit of trust with our regional, European, and international partners.

items.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
items.summary: Ameth Bek Hospital in Abyei town has been treating people wounded in Monday's attack on the market Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011 South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest.

items.title: Is Ebola under control in Kenya after nine cases confirmed?
items.summary: Nearly 5,000 healthcare workers have been trained to deal with Ebola Kenya is grappling with its first ever outbreak of Ebola, a disease which neighbouring countries, such as Uganda and Democratic Republic of Congo, are used to dealing with Nine cases have now been confirmed including its first patient, who travelled from DR Congo and died two weeks ago Four relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner have now tested positive, meaning they are all linked to him But concerns are rising that the virus could start spreading further, even as the government has sought to assure citizens The US has warned it citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert Kenyans have been expressing their concerns that the disease could spread more widely More than 4,000 people have died since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease With more than 9,500 cases in DR Congo, Kenya faces a steady risk of new cases arriving across borders, according…
